findings.detail: The divergence reproduces exactly: run state {intro_shown: true} with no intake_purpose_flow, no flow markers and no answers -> factory.py _purpose_flow_for/_run_is_new classifies PURPOSE ('Question 1 of 15') while intake_card.new_run_flow classifies OFFER ('Question 1 of 14'). Reachability refined against the whole repo: the only intro_shown writers are card_session_cli._intro (which always writes intake_purpose_flow in the same atomic replace) and intro.take() (which writes intro_shown alone). intro.take()'s sole caller, intake_card.py main line 1653, is unreachable in the shipped CLI: every run-bound invocation (run_dir or run_state_file or session-json or seed) diverts to card_session_cli.run at lines 1646-1649 before the a.step branch, and inside that branch a.run_state_file is always empty so the _intro_take call can never fire. So no current writer of THIS tree produces the state; the builder's 'only reachable from pre-upgrade run states, nothing to migrate' stands for the canonical tree, with the caveat that the single-field writer still exists (dead branch here, live if an out-of-tree adapter calls intro.take -- adapter-repo parity was not checked by builder or QC). The unit docstring claim 'the API and the launcher can never disagree' is therefore true for every state current code writes, not literally true for all states.

test_the_api_and_the_launcher_agree_on_the_default compares IC.main against IC.conversation only; factory.py card is not driven by any single test at that assertion level. Confirmed in the test source (lines 195-213). Evidence gap partially closed by this lane: the launcher (factory.py card) was driven directly in every acceptance scenario (fresh/resumed/purpose-marker) and in the E2E method.json run, agreeing with the API default in all states current code writes; the only disagreement remains the F1 dead-state (see F2_cross_entry_point_probe).
